These satoshis, once just units of value, now become carriers of meaning. A satx can hold a timestamp, a message, a license, a declaration—anything that must be recorded permanently and provably. And it doesn’t point somewhere else for that information. The content is on-chain, fixed in the Bitcoin ledger itself. This structure transforms the satoshi into more than a monetary fragment—it becomes a self-verifying certificate. Possessing the satx means possessing its embedded proof. No signature needed. No API to check. No interface to trust. Whether it’s proving the date of a digital artwork, the origin of a supply chain item, or the execution of a community vote, the satx stands as an unchangeable record—resistant to time, censorship, and manipulation. Unlike smart contract platforms, satx doesn’t rely on execution logic. It’s not about programmability in the traditional sense. It’s about inscription—the act of anchoring meaning to a permanent, neutral ledger. That gives it a unique strength: compatibility with any system that needs high-integrity data, whether it’s a DAO operating on Ethereum, a decentralized ID system on Polkadot, or a machine-learning agent filtering signals. satx also prepares Bitcoin for the machine-readable future. As autonomous systems grow, they will require inputs that are not just data-rich, but verifiably correct at origin. satx delivers this—digital facts with cryptographic proof, embedded directly at the base layer of the most trusted network on Earth. ALLO : The Lifeblood of Allora’s Intelligent Economy AlloraNetwork is building something powerful — a decentralized system where anyone can request predictions, contribute AI models, and improve outcomes over time. At the center of this system is the ALLO. It’s not just a cryptocurrency. It’s the fuel that keeps the network running, growing, and learning. let’s break down how ALLO is used, in the simplest way possible. 1. You Choose the Price: Pay-What-You-Want Allora does something very different. When you ask the network for a prediction (called an “inference”), you choose how much you want to pay using ALLO tokens. This model is called Pay-What-You-Want (PWYW). How it works: -If you pay more ALLO → your request gets more attention, and contributors are rewarded. -If you pay nothing → the topic becomes inactive over time, and no one earns rewards from it. This keeps the network fair and demand-driven. You’re not forced to pay a fixed price ��� instead, you pay based on how valuable the answer is to you. 2. Creating and Joining Topics Allora is organized into topics. Each topic is a specific area where predictions are made — like “Bitcoin price in 5 minutes” or “Ethereum gas fees tomorrow.” To participate in a topic, whether as: a Worker (someone who submits predictions), or a Reputer (someone who scores predictions), …you need to pay a small fee in ALLO to register. This helps filter out spam and makes sure only serious participants join. It also gives the topic weight, which affects how much reward it can attract. 3. Staking & Delegation: Earn by Supporting the Network ALLO is also used for staking — which means locking up tokens to support the network and earn rewards. Here’s how it works: -Reputers stake ALLO to prove they are trustworthy. -Validators stake ALLO to help secure the network. -Regular users can delegate their ALLO to a reputer or validator and earn a share of the rewards. Staking creates trust and accountability. The more ALLO someone has at stake, the more careful they are about doing quality work. 4. Earning Rewards in ALLO Everyone who helps the network gets paid in ALLO: -Workers earn when their predictions are accurate. -Reputers earn for giving fair scores. -Validators earn for maintaining honest consensus. -Delegators earn a portion of the rewards from the people they support. Where do these rewards come from? -A portion comes from inference payments (PWYW). -The rest comes from newly released ALLO tokens through emissions. 5. Emissions and Long-Term Value ALLO tokens are released over time in a schedule similar to Bitcoin’s halving model. This means: -Fewer new tokens are released as time goes on. -Early participants are rewarded more. -The supply is limited and predictable. Allora also makes sure that rewards stay stable, even when tokens unlock. This prevents big price drops and encourages people to stake long-term instead of selling quickly. ALLO is More Than Just a Token ALLO is what keeps the AlloraNetwork alive and evolving. It’s how users show what they value. It’s how contributors are paid fairly. It’s how reputation, trust, and incentives stay aligned.

GhostDAG, a proof-of-work consensus protocol that generalizes Nakamoto’s chain into a directed acyclic graph of blocks ( blockDAG). GhostDAG incorporates”orphan” blocks into the chain to form a blockDAG, and then uses a novel greedy algorithm to order the blocks such that well-connected, honest blocks are favored, quickly and with high probability. GhostDAG allows Kaspa to circumvent the traditional tradeoff of blockchains, improving on block rate by orders of magnitude while maintaining the theoretical security guarantees of Bitcoin. The DAGKNIGHT Protocol, written by Michael Sutton and Yonatan Sompolinsky, is a three-year work of genius and consensus upgrade for Kaspa’s PHANTOM GHOSTDAG Protocol. KNIGHT was set in motion with the goal of resisting 50% attacks without knowing the network latency ahead of time. Typically, blockchain protocols assume a parameter of network delay for best and/or worst-case scenarios without the ability to adapt to real-time latency. This assumed latency parameter keeps blockchains restrained to slower confirmation times to avoid security risks and instability. A 50% or 51% attack occurs when a group or entity owns more than 50% of the nodes on the network, granting the controlling parties the ability to alter the blockchain. However, with network delay left unaddressed, if latency spikes, the percentage of ownership needed for an attack decreases. Subsequently leaving the chain more susceptible to an attack. To fix this, blockchains sacrifice block confirmation time to account for the ailing network health by setting an estimated/assumed network delay parameter.

Alas, the world will be boring. A primer on why there won't be an USD MOASS. This is a discussion in three parts. 1. There won't be a MOASS because there just isn't enough shorts. 2. No, foreign banks are not net short on the dollar, so when they are stressed, they are not buying dollars. 3. Between the Fed and the treasury, neither of them want a MOASS, and they have the tools to nip this in the bud. Part 1: No shorts First, let's talk about the boring parts: no, there just isn't the shorts needed for a MOASS to work. Mechanically, net trade balances are the same as net investment flows. Americans buy a pile of stuff from foreigners, pays dollars for them, and the foreigners now have a pile of dollars. If they try to sell the dollars for their own domestic currencies, then this will push the dollar down against various currencies, and then the trade imbalance will go away via supply and demand of the dollar. Of course, this isn't happening, and it doesn't happen: American trade balances are consistently negative, which means that not only are foreigners consistently long on the dollar, they are getting longer and longer every single year. This year, after the "liberation day" tariffs, DXY took a nose-dive as foreigners sold their investments. But trade data was still negative in April; a lot less negative than previously, but still very negative. So even at current levels of DXY, foreigners are getting longer, just somewhat slower. There is probably a point in DXY where foreigners are net neutral, but we are pretty far from it, and the entire post WW2 order of US trade deficits will take a while to work through. Part 2: Foreign Bankers, and how they will be net dollar sellers in a crisis yieldsearcher below puts out an interesting thesis here: the crisis will be started by liquidations of foreign investors. The theory goes something like this: Japan is filled with Mrs. Watanabes, who is borrowing JPY to buy USTs (or NDX or SPX, it doesn't really matter). As DXY falls, Mrs Watanabe will be facing a margin call, many of them will default, and then Japanese banks will come under pressure, where they will need to buy dollars. Here is the problem: they will be net sellers! The big Japanese banks not only have liabilities in dollars, they also have liabilities in Yen. And as Mrs. Watanabes gets liquidated one after another, our Japanese banks will be having trouble getting their JPY based loans getting paid back, and they will be getting extra dollars that they will be looking to get rid of. Not only are they not buyers, they are sellers, which will of course make the crisis worse. Part 3: The mechanics of a Dollar MOASS, or why the Fed will be squash the thing in the bud, should it get going. A clever reader will no doubt realize that I am skilling past the proposed catalysts, the Genius Act and OBBB. I am unsure how exactly the remittance tax will work, but here, I will describe how and why the Fed and Trump admin will be forced to quickly act to quash such an event, should it happen. The main problem with the Dollar MOASS is that foreigners don't just hold t-bills. They hold things like stocks, bonds, real estate, Bitcoin, and so on. And in any short squeeze, they will be selling whatever they can get to keep the margin calls away. And so, in a true Dollar MOASS, you won't just see the DXY shoot up: the SPX will be crashing, the treasury will be completely unable to sell treasury bonds, and so on. And since there are domestic leveraged investors too, this whole thing can and will turn into a cascading margin call situation. Trump may or may not need to care about foreigners, but he needs the financial system alive. Companies need to issue bonds to make payroll, the treasury needs to be funded (through they can always resort to t-bills when push comes to shove), and so on. And so, the Fed will be forced to unleash the floodgates, and since dollars are fungible, any bailout of the domestic financial system will also bailout the foreign one.

USR maintains price stability by leveraging the combined strengths of Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH), the two largest cryptocurrencies. What makes Resolv unique is its Resolv Liquidity Protocol (RLP), an innovative liquidity and insurance layer. Unlike over-collateralized stablecoins, RLP facilitates capital efficiency and stability through a unique risk management and yield generation structure. The main objective of Resolv is to enable stablecoins to operate independently of fiat currency and use only cryptocurrencies as collateral. The platform’s USR stablecoin has been engineered to maintain a 1:1 USD peg using unique delta-neutral strategies designed to counteract price volatility by being backed by cryptocurrencies. Key Features of Resolv Resolv Protocol stands out with a unique mechanism designed to maintain the token stability and counter crypto market volatility. Users can deposit Bitcoin or Ethereum as collateral to mint USR, while Resolv simultaneously opens several short perpetual positions using BTC and ETH. The Resolv Liquidity Pool (RLP) is another advanced feature of the Resolv protocol, where users can stake tokens to support the system and earn high yields. Union is called the "blockchain of blockchains" because it aims to unify multiple blockchain networks into a single, interoperable ecosystem. It enables seamless communication, data sharing, and transaction processing across different blockchains, addressing fragmentation and scalability issues. By acting as a layer that connects different chains, it creates a cohesive framework, much like a blockchain that integrates other blockchains. It achieves its "blockchain of blockchains" status through a combination of technical features designed to enable interoperability and scalability across multiple blockchain networks. Here's how it works: Interoperability Protocol: Union Build uses a cross-chain communication protocol that allows different blockchains (e.g., Ethereum, Bitcoin, or newer chains like Monad which is coming soon) to exchange data and value securely. This is often facilitated by bridges or relayers that translate and validate transactions between chains. Unified Settlement Layer: It provides a layer where transactions from various blockchains can be finalized or settled, reducing the need for each chain to process independently. This acts like a hub that coordinates activity across networks. Modular Architecture: Union Build's design is modular, enabling it to integrate with diverse blockchain architectures (public, private, or consortium) without requiring them to change their native protocols. Scalability Solutions: By aggregating transactions and processing them through optimized mechanisms (like rollups or sharding), it enhances throughput and reduces congestion on individual chains. Decentralized Governance: A decentralized framework ensures trust and security, allowing participating chains to maintain sovereignty while collaborating within the Union ecosystem. We can call it a universal adapter that connects isolated blockchain "islands" into a cohesive network, enabling them to function as a single, scalable system. Let's talk a little bit about boundless_xyz fam Described as the “first universal ZK protocol,” Boundless aims to bring ZK capabilities to all blockchains (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, etc.) without requiring new chains or migrations. This cross-chain composability is seen as a game-changer, enabling seamless integration and unified liquidity across ecosystems. Now let's break this down further in plain English In simple terms, a ZK protocol (short for Zero-Knowledge protocol) is a tech tool that let's blockchains (like Bitcoin, Ethereum, or Solana) prove something is true without revealing extra details. Think of it like proving you’re over 21 years of age without showing your entire ID, just the part that confirms your age. What Boundless does: It’s a system that let's all blockchains use the ZK tech. Normally, blockchains work separately, like different apps that don’t talk to each other. Boundless makes it so they can work together smoothly, without anyone needing to build a new blockchain or move their stuff to a different one. Why it’s a big deal: This “cross-chain composability” means blockchains can share resources, like money or data, easily. JAM (Join-Accumulate Machine), the next evolution, reimagines Polkadot as an architecture that doesn’t just secure blockchains but any Web3 app. Think decentralized AI. Smart cities. The combined global equity and debt markets currently total around $415 trillion. A modest rotation of just 0.1% of this capital into Bitcoin would represent approximately $415 billion in new investment. Analyst thomas_fahrer estimates a reflexivity multiplier of around 10x in this context. Applying this multiplier to the $415 billion inflow suggests a potential $4.15 trillion increase in Bitcoin market capitalization. This phenomenon, known in economics as “reflexivity,” describes how rising prices attract more investors, which in turn drives prices even higher through a reinforcing feedback loop. This dynamic underpins the flywheel effect famously demonstrated by MicroStrategy’s Bitcoin accumulation strategy. Real-World Performance and Market Evidence Linekong Interactive Group: Holds 44 BTC (~$4.6M value), with a 164x stock price gain since announcing BTC treasury strategy still undervalued based on BTC reserves. Market Mechanics Bitcoin treasury stocks often trade at premiums above their Bitcoin-backed mNAV, allowing companies to raise fresh capital at attractive valuations. They use this capital to accumulate more Bitcoin, reducing circulating supply and driving prices higher. As BTC prices rise, so do the value of their reserves and stock prices, creating a self-reinforcing flywheel. Historically, after such BTC-driven growth, capital tends to rotate out of Bitcoin into Ethereum and then altcoins kicking off the next altcoin season. This cycle now has a new twist: PVC / Public Bitcoin treasury stocks will channel capital before it flows into altcoins. Its incentives (Proof-of-Work, a fixed supply schedule, and globally distributed nodes) make hostile takeovers uneconomical and make changes virtually impossible without broad, voluntary consensus. Everything else in “crypto” functions more like equity in a startup: centrally issued, centrally steered, centrally upgraded. That can be fine for speculative tech, but it cannot serve as neutral, permissionless money. Bitcoin’s architecture, by contrast, replicates gold’s scarcity and cash’s finality while adding instant global settlement and auditable transparency. The consequences are profound: individuals gain a savings technology that can’t be inflated away, and societies gain a non-political base layer for value transfer. This is why at relai_app we remain Bitcoin-only. If the mission is sound, censorship-resistant money, there is no substitute.

What is Anoma anoma and why should you care? Think of a new town where blockchains are like freshly paved roads, each one hyped as the future. Bitcoin laid the first street, then Ethereum, Solana, and others followed, each with a new twist. But where’s the buzz—the apps that make this town worth visiting? Web3 feels like a quiet place with lots of roads but few shops or hangouts. Developers struggle to pick the “right” blockchain to build on, and users get bogged down by a tangle of wallets, bridges, and tricky steps just to swap tokens or buy something. The issue is everything’s split apart - fragmentation. Each new blockchain divides Web3 further, scattering users, apps, and money across separate networks. Developers pour time and cash into building for one chain, only to see users flock to another, like playing musical chairs. For users, it’s a hassle—managing multiple wallets and slogging through complex steps feels like cracking a code to send a payment. This keeps Web3 stuck on building tech instead of apps that could be as easy as your phone’s favorites. Anoma’s like a friendly guide who ties this scattered Web3 town together, linking blockchains—Ethereum, Solana, and beyond—into one simple system. It lets developers build one app that works on any chain, no need to guess which one will take off. With “intents,” users just say what they want, like “swap token X for Y,” and Anoma handles the complicated stuff quietly in the background. This cuts down time and costs for developers, so they can focus on making apps as smooth and familiar as Web2 hits like Uber or Kickstarter, but fully decentralized and free from any central control. Anoma makes this happen with three parts: Application Layer: A space where developers create easy apps by stating goals, using an “intent machine” that skips the need to code every little step. Networking Layer: A network of nodes that shares user requests and uses solvers to handle them, even for tricky deals like swapping tokens across chains. Settlement Layer: The part that wraps up transactions on any blockchain, tying them together so apps work anywhere without users seeing the techy details. By putting apps first instead of more tech, Anoma could make Web3 a lively spot where everyone, not just crypto fans, wants to hang out.

Plus, Boundless can bundle multiple proofs to save cost and cut redundancy. Built for Devs: You don’t need to be a ZK wizard. Why Bridges Are Broken and How Portal to Bitcoin Fixes It. Cross-chain bridges, designed to connect blockchains like Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana, have been a cornerstone of DeFi’s promise of interoperability. However, they’re riddled with flaws that undermine their reliability and security, leaving users vulnerable. PortaltoBitcoin offers a groundbreaking solution by enabling trustless, custody-free swaps of native Bitcoin, Ordinals, and Runes across chains, bypassing the pitfalls of traditional bridges. The Problem with Bridges Bridges often rely on custodial or semi-custodial models, requiring users to lock assets in smart contracts or trust third parties, creating single points of failure. These vulnerabilities have led to catastrophic hacks—over $2 billion was stolen in bridge attacks since 2021, including the $320 million Wormhole exploit in 2022 and the $570 million BNB Chain hack. Even trustless bridges, which use smart contracts, aren’t immune. Poorly audited code or validator collusion can lead to exploits, while wrapped tokens like wBTC introduce additional risks, as they depend on custodians like BitGo to hold native BTC. Bridges also suffer from high fees during network congestion and slow transaction times, sometimes taking hours, which frustrates users seeking seamless DeFi access. Moreover, the complexity of lock-and-mint or burn-and-mint mechanisms alienates non-technical users, hindering mass adoption. Portal to Bitcoin’s Solution PortaltoBitcoin redefines cross-chain DeFi by eliminating bridges altogether. Instead of wrapping assets or relying on custodians, it uses atomic swaps powered by Multi-Party Hash Time-Locked Contracts (MP-HTLCs). This allows users to swap native BTC directly with assets on chains like Ethereum or Solana without intermediaries, ensuring full custody and security. The process is simple: funds are locked in an HTLC on the source chain (e.g., Bitcoin), and a matching HTLC on the destination chain (e.g., Ethereum) ensures the swap either completes or reverts, minimizing risk. The Portal Wallet enhances this experience with a self-custodial design, letting users retain control of their assets while swapping across chains. Integrated with RAFA, an AI guide, it simplifies complex DeFi flows, making cross-chain interactions accessible to beginners. Unlike static wallets, Portal’s dynamic infrastructure acts as a gateway and coordinator, enabling native BTC to flow into DeFi ecosystems without compromising Bitcoin’s principles of decentralization and security. Security and Scalability Portal’s Notary Chain, secured by a Threshold Signature Scheme (TSS), ensures no single validator can compromise funds, reducing trust assumptions compared to traditional bridges. This decentralized validator system contrasts with custodial bridges’ vulnerabilities, like those seen in the Ronin hack, where $625 million was stolen due to centralized control. By avoiding wrapped tokens, Portal eliminates the risks of unbacked assets or custodian failures. Its architecture also supports scalability, handling swaps efficiently without the congestion issues plaguing bridges like Polygon or Avalanche during peak times. The Future of Bitcoin in DeFi With Bitcoin’s DeFi TVL at $1.9 billion compared to Ethereum’s $47.5 billion, the potential for growth is massive. Portal to Bitcoin unlocks this by enabling native BTC to participate in yield farming, lending, and staking across chains without risky intermediaries. Backed by Coinbase and OKX, with $42M raised, Portal’s Aurelia Testnet incentivizes users with 8.4B P tokens for running LiteNodes, fostering a robust ecosystem. In a multi-chain world, bridges are broken—prone to hacks, high costs, and complexity. PortaltoBitcoin offers a trustless, user-friendly alternative, making native Bitcoin a dynamic player in DeFi while staying true to its decentralized ethos.

Worried about quantum computers breaking Bitcoin? Take a look at your credit card first... “What if a quantum computer hacks Bitcoin?” is a fair question, but based on a misunderstanding of how secure Bitcoin actually is. Today’s Bitcoin addresses are protected not just by ECDSA (the signature system), but by SHA-256 and RIPEMD-160 hashes as well (to infer a private key from a public address). Let's put it in context, your credit card relies on: A 16-digit card number (≈ 10¹⁶ possibilities) A 4-digit PIN (10⁴ possibilities) That’s a total search space of roughly 10²⁰ combinations. Now compare that with Bitcoin: SHA-256 = 2²⁵⁶ ≈ 10⁷⁷ RIPEMD-160 = 2¹⁶⁰ ≈ 10⁴⁸ So even RIPEMD-160 offers a space 10²⁸ times (10⁴⁸ / 10²⁰ = 10²⁸) larger than your credit card, and for SHA-256, it's 10⁵⁷ times larger. Crucially, until you spend from an address, your public key isn’t revealed, so a UTXO on an address that has never spent is even more secure. To infer a private key from a public address (not "from a public key" because the public key has not been shared yet), one would need to crack both the SHA-256 and the RIPEMD-160 algorithms together, multiplying these two search spaces. Quantum threats are real, but they’ll hit legacy systems, like the traditional payment networks, long before they threaten Bitcoin. And when the time comes, Bitcoin will adapt to become quantum resistant. So, no, Bitcoin isn't the weak link. Not even close.

It “reinforces that US courts may assert jurisdiction if the alleged misconduct involves US-based communications, personnel or financial accounts.” In short, New York Judge Martin Glenn’s ruling isn’t necessarily about who owes what, but the signal it sends to companies residing outside of the US. It’s a warning shot to those firms that they aren’t out of reach of American courts just because they’re incorporated in other jurisdictions. It also arrives as Washington inches closer to passing landmark stablecoin legislation in the US. With the $263 billion sector under growing scrutiny, the case could shape how US courts interpret oversight and accountability, particularly for firms like Tether that operate across borders but touch US systems. Celsius went bankrupt in 2022 after a series of crypto scandals led jittery users to withdraw their crypto in massive amounts. The company was unable to honour those withdrawals and declared bankruptcy in June 2022. In May this year, Celsius CEO Alex Mashinky received a 12-year prison sentence. “Although the Court determined that it could not dismiss the case in its entirety prior to discovery, Celsius’ claims on the merits remain as baseless today as they were when first filed,” a Tether representative told DL News. “We look forward to proving that in court.” Representatives for Celsius didn’t respond to requests for comment. Allegations The case stems from the 2022 crypto crash, when Celsius pledged 39,500 Bitcoin as collateral for a USDT loan from Tether. The loan, worth approximately $820 million at the time, came with a 10-hour grace period in the event of a margin call. But when Bitcoin prices plunged amid a systemic collapse brought on by the implosion of the stablecoin project Terra, Tether allegedly liquidated Celsius’ collateral after just nine hours and sold Bitcoin at a low of about $20,000. Celsius alleged the early liquidation breached the loan agreement and gave Tether unfair repayment priority over other creditors. Importantly, if the lawsuit is successful, it could compel stablecoin issuers and lenders to tighten their contracts and reconsider how liquidations are triggered under market stress. Most Web3 apps today are confined to individual chains, which limits their flexibility and composability. Anoma changes this by introducing a new way to build apps. They simply express what they want. For example: “I want to reserve a hotel room under $100 and pay using either reward tokens or USDC.” That’s an intent, not a transaction. The app interprets your goal instead of requiring you to follow a rigid process. 𝟐. 𝐒𝐨𝐥𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐍𝐞𝐭𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤 A distributed mesh of solver agents identifies the intent and finds viable paths to fulfill it, such as swapping tokens, verifying availability, or completing a booking. They bundle everything into a valid transaction. You don't manage the steps—solvers coordinate them for you. They only get paid if the intent is successfully fulfilled. 𝟑. 𝐅𝐥𝐞𝐱𝐢𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐒𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 Once solved, the result can be finalized on any chain: Ethereum, Solana, Bitcoin, or even your own private instance. Anoma doesn’t force settlement on a single layer — it lets you choose based on speed, privacy, or security needs. In short: anoma unbundles execution, coordination, and settlement. Ever seen BVS pop up on SatLayer tweets and scratched your head? You're not alone. Let's unravel what this digital guardian is all about. What is a BVS? Let’s assume there is a busy digital marketplace where things happen super fast, sometimes even off the main blockchain. How do you ensure everyone plays fair? That's where a BVS (Bitcoin Verifiable System) comes in. BVS feature as a super smart, self policing security guard for these off chain operations. It's built on a simple but powerful idea where BTCFI talks. How Does This Digital Guardian Work? The Pledge (Your Digital Bond): ◦Node operators which are the digital workers handling transactions put up a financial pledge or bond. This is their stake. It's like putting down a security deposit. The Rulebook (Slashing Conditions): ◦Every BVS has a clear set of slashing conditions. These are like strict rules: Don't cheat, Don't be lazy, Don't cause problems. These rules can be coded directly into the blockchain or monitored externally. The Consequence (The Slashing Bite): ◦If a node operator breaks a rule, the BVS slashes them. This means a portion, or even all, of their pledged assets are confiscated. ◦Where does the lost money go? It can be sent to those who helped secure the system called Vault restakers as a reward, or it can be permanently burned , sending a clear message. Why This System is Brilliant: No one wants to lose their hardearned crypto. This financial risk strongly discourages bad behavior, making node operators super careful and trustworthy. Restakers are people who lend their crypto to support these node operators. They are motivated to pick only the most reliable operators and keep an eye out for any shady moves. Why? Because their own assets are tied to the operators' good conduct, and they earn rewards for smart choices. Building these systems is complex. The BVS developers have to make sure that slashing is: ◦Affordable: Easy and cheap enough to execute so bad actors can't just overwhelm the system. ◦Secure: Impossible to misuse or trigger accidentally with false accusations. •Your Rewards for Trust: By accepting the risk of potentially losing assets if an operator misbehaves, restakers earn rewards. These rewards, distributed through the SatLayer ecosystem, can be in the BVS own token or other specified cryptocurrencies. So, when you see BVS on SatLayer, know that it's all about building a robust, financially incentivized system to ensure trust and security in the fast evolving world of off chain digital interactions. gSAT

Understanding Key Technologies Behind PortaltoBitcoin ’s Trustless DeFi HTLC (Hash Time-Locked Contract): A fundamental cryptographic smart contract enabling secure, trustless cross chain atomic swaps. HTLCs function as conditional escrows where Party A locks funds using a cryptographic hash (secret). Party B must reveal the matching secret within a specified time frame to claim the funds; otherwise, the assets revert to Party A after timeout. This mechanism ensures atomicity either both sides complete the swap or none do eliminating the need for intermediaries and preserving decentralization critical for Bitcoin DeFi. MPHTLC (Multi-Party HTLC): An advanced innovation by Portal to Bitcoin that extends traditional HTLCs to facilitate simultaneous multi-party atomic swaps within a single transaction. Leveraging policy scripts and optimized Bitcoin transaction structures, MPHTLCs batch multiple cross-chain swaps to improve execution efficiency, reduce on-chain fees, and enhance privacy by minimizing visible data on the blockchain. This design is pivotal for scaling complex Bitcoin DeFi interactions securely. BitScaler: Portal’s off-chain coordination engine that powers Portal OS by orchestrating MPHTLCs. BitScaler optimizes liquidity routing across diverse blockchains, manages atomicity verification, and coordinates multi-party transaction execution off-chain. This reduces congestion and on-chain resource usage on Bitcoin’s Layer 1 while ensuring final settlement remains trustless and secure fully aligned with Bitcoin’s sovereignty principles and without reliance on custodians or bridges. Taproot: A significant Bitcoin protocol upgrade activated in 2021 that improves privacy, efficiency, and programmability of smart contracts. Utilizing Schnorr signatures and Merkelized Abstract Syntax Trees (MAST), Taproot enables complex contract logic such as MPHTLC scripts to appear indistinguishable from regular transactions. Validity Proofs on GOAT Network On goatnetwork, validity proofs are used to make sure that off-chain (Layer 2) transactions are secure and correct before being locked in on the Bitcoin main chain (Layer 1). This setup removes the need for trust and gives users a decentralized way to verify transactions. 1/ Proof Creation GOAT uses ZKM (Zero-Knowledge Machine) to build validity proofs. Tasks are split and handled by different provers: Root Prover makes the first proof Aggregation Prover combines multiple proofs SNARK Prover turns the final result into a Groth16 proof (small and fast for on-chain use) 2/ Proof Posting Once finished, the final proof is submitted to the Bitcoin blockchain for public verification. 3/ Challenge System If someone suspects the proof is wrong, they can challenge it using the Optimistic Challenge Protocol. If the challenge is valid, the original proof is canceled and the transaction gets rolled back. If the challenge fails, the proof stands, and the transaction is finalized.

Here's an overview of the Alkanes protocol and the various projects working on it. What is the Alkanes protocol? Alkanes is a metaprotocol that allows developers to create and run smart contracts compiled to WebAssembly (WASM) directly on the Bitcoin blockchain. Unlike traditional solutions like the Lightning Network or sidechains, Alkanes leverages Bitcoin's native capabilities to integrate complex features while preserving the network's immutability and robustness. This protocol leverages innovations like registrations (introduced by the Ordinals protocol) to store additional data on the blockchain, enabling the creation of unique digital assets and executable programs. The protocol features: - **Direct deployment on Bitcoin L1**: No need for external solutions, reducing the risks associated with bridges or secondary layers. - **Scalable smart contracts**: WASM contracts provide flexibility for building diverse applications. - **Compatibility with the Bitcoin ecosystem**: Alkanes integrates with existing protocols like Runes and Ordinals, enhancing scalability. Projects Associated with the Alkanes Protocol Since its launch in 2025, Alkanes has garnered significant interest from the Bitcoin community, spawning several promising projects in various fields, including decentralized finance (DeFi), NFTs, and asset management tools. Here are some notable examples: 1. Satonomy: A platform for viewing and managing UTXOs (Unspent Transaction Outputs) that integrates Alkanes tokens and exclusive access, such as “OG cards” similar to VIP passes. Satonomy is positioned as one of the first projects to leverage Alkanes for practical applications, offering tools for managing digital assets on Bitcoin. Initiatives like the “Beep Boop” collection have garnered attention for their community-driven approach and whitelisting (WL) opportunities. 2. Yala: This project combines the security of Bitcoin with a modular framework to connect BTC holders to DeFi protocols on other blockchains. Yala uses a stablecoin called YU as a medium of exchange and store of value, allowing users to generate returns from their Bitcoins via decentralized applications. Alkanes plays a key role in facilitating these integrations directly on Bitcoin L1.[]( 3. **NFTs and inscription collections**: Alkanes enables the creation of NFTs directly on Bitcoin, building on the success of Ordinals. Projects like “Pizza Ninjas” (inscriptions of large files occupying entire blocks, called “four meggers”) illustrate how Alkanes can be used to create unique digital assets, valued for their visibility and rarity on the blockchain. These projects attract collectors due to their exclusivity. 4. Fungible Tokens (similar to BRC-20): Alkanes is inspired by the BRC-20 protocol, which popularized fungible tokens on Bitcoin through Ordinal inscriptions. Token projects based on Alkanes are emerging, offering an alternative to traditional models like ORDI, with Fair Launch mechanisms to encourage community participation. 5. DeFi Experiments: Alkanes is paving the way for DeFi applications directly on Bitcoin, a field historically dominated by blockchains like Ethereum. The Fraud of Fiat – Explained for the Everyman Let’s say you’re playing Monopoly. The banker can print as much money as they want — and they do, every time the game gets tough. Eventually, the board is flooded with cash, prices go up, and no one trusts the money anymore. That’s fiat currency in a nutshell. Fiat = "By decree" — not backed by anything real (like gold or oil), only by government orders and public belief. It’s created as debt. Every dollar printed is loaned into existence, with interest. That means we can never pay it all back — mathematically impossible. Central banks control it. A few unelected elites decide when to print more, who gets it first (hint: it ain’t you), and how much you’ll lose in purchasing power. You’re taxed when you earn (income tax), when you spend (sales tax), when you save (inflation tax), and when you die (estate tax). All while your dollar buys less year after year. Why People Don’t See the Scam (Yet) Normalcy Bias: People assume what’s always been, will always be. They’re born into this game and never question the rules. Complexity Theater: The financial system is made to sound too complicated for you to understand. That’s on purpose. Bread & Circuses: Distract with culture wars, Netflix, and TikTok while the wealth is siphoned upward through monetary policy. Short-Term Gratification: Fiat feeds instant pleasure — credit cards, buy-now-pay-later, stimulus checks — while hiding long-term consequences. Bitcoin: The Fire Exit from the Fiat Theater Bitcoin is the first tool in history that separates money from state control, just like the printing press separated truth from the church. What makes it revolutionary: Fixed Supply: Only 21 million Bitcoin ever — no central bank can print more. Inflation? Capped. Permission less: Anyone, anywhere can use it. No need to ask a bank, government, or corporation. Decentralized: No CEO, no headquarters, no off switch. Run by thousands of nodes around the globe. Transparent: Every transaction is auditable on the blockchain. No hidden bailouts. Borderless: Value that moves like email — unstoppable. So Why Isn’t Everyone Using It Yet? Volatility – Because it’s still early. Bitcoin is transitioning from infancy (speculative store of value) to adolescence (medium of exchange). Like early internet stocks, it’s volatile until adoption stabilizes. Regulatory Roadblocks – Governments fear losing monetary control. They try to slow it down, confuse the public, or launch distractions like CBDCs. Education Gap – Most people still think Bitcoin is "just an investment." They haven’t yet seen it as a parallel system of money. What Needs to Happen for the Masses to Wake Up More Currency Crises: When fiat collapses (Argentina, Turkey, Lebanon…), people wake up fast. Eventually, even USD will lose dominance. Opt-out Infrastructure: Easy tools — like Strike, Muun, Phoenix, or Cashu wallets — that let users send sats like Venmo but without middlemen. Narrative Shift: From "Bitcoin = risky investment" to "Bitcoin = life raft from inflation and surveillance." Community Nodes: Local adoption through education, circular economies, and merchant acceptance. Bottom-up, not top-down. Will Bitcoin Become a Medium of Exchange? Yes — but in phases: Phase 1: Store of Value (like gold) – Where we are now. Phase 2: Medium of Exchange – Already happening in El Salvador, parts of Africa, and among Bitcoiners globally. Phase 3: Unit of Account – When goods and salaries are denominated in sats (e.g., 100,000 sats instead of $35). The Lightning Network and new privacy protocols (like Fedimint or Cashu) are making Bitcoin practical for daily use. Slowly but surely, it’s happening. Final Thought: “The root problem with conventional currency is all the trust that’s required to make it work.” – Satoshi Nakamoto Bitcoin removes the need for trust in corrupt institutions. It’s not just better money — it’s a peaceful revolution. The moment the average worker, parent, or business owner sees that their savings are being silently stolen through inflation, and that a fairer system already exists, Bitcoin stops being a curiosity and becomes a necessity. Until then, the job is ours: To show the exit. One mind at a time.

A mesh network is a type of communication system where each device (or “node”) connects directly to others nearby. Instead of relying on a central server or a single router, devices pass information between each other in a web-like pattern. This creates a self-healing and decentralized network that can still function even if some parts go down. How It Works for Electronic Cash Here's how mesh networks can be used to transmit peer-to-peer money like eCash: 1. Offline Transaction Signing The user creates and signs a transaction on their device without internet. This signed transaction is a cryptographic message authorizing the movement of eCash from one wallet to another. 2. Broadcast via Bluetooth or Wi-Fi Direct The transaction is sent using short-range communication, such as Bluetooth or local Wi-Fi. This ensures that even in remote or disconnected areas, two users can exchange digital money. 3. Relay Through Other Nodes If the initial device isn't connected to the broader network, it can pass the transaction along to other nearby devices until it reaches one with internet access, which then broadcasts it to the blockchain. 4. Encryption & Privacy Using end-to-end encryption (e.g., Curve25519), the transaction remains secure and tamper-proof during its offline journey. It’s censorship-resistant by nature. Real-World Tools & Projects Projects like Bitcoin-Mesh and apps like Bitchat have demonstrated how this works. By modifying or forking these open-source tools, similar methods could be applied to the eCash protocol or integrated into Xolos RMZ wallets. Community Implications For communities that embrace values of sovereignty, privacy, and resilience, mesh networks represent a return to the spirit of electronic cash envisioned in the early Bitcoin whitepaper: a system for peer-to-peer payments without trusted third parties. What makes Portal different? → You swap BTC for ETH → No vaults → No LP tokens → No bridges → No wrapped assets The trade either happens or doesn’t. No halfway No risk in between. Portal swaps would’ve prevented that entirely. There’s no contract holding pooled funds. There’s no “mint” or “redeem” function to manipulate. There’s no delay to exploit. There’s no system to fake. Understanding the Key Difference Between Lido and Lombard. ◾ Technical Approach: Lido and Lombard_Finance are both liquid staking platforms, but they serve fundamentally different blockchains and operate under contrasting assumptions due to the nature of their underlying consensus mechanisms. Lido is designed for Ethereum, a Proof-of-Stake (PoS) network. When users stake ETH via Lido, they receive stETH, a liquid representation of their staked tokens. This token accrues rewards over time and remains usable in DeFi protocols, enabling users to earn while maintaining liquidity. Lombard_Finance, on the other hand, brings liquid staking to Bitcoin, which is not a PoS blockchain. Bitcoin operates under Proof-of-Work (PoW) and does not support native staking. Lombard solves this by introducing LBTC, a liquid, yield-bearing version of BTC that is staked indirectly through the Babylon protocol. This allows Bitcoin holders to earn rewards in PoS environments while still preserving their Bitcoin exposure. Essentially, Lido enhances utility for a PoS-native asset, while Lombard_Finance introduces an entirely new staking layer to a PoW-native asset, bridging Bitcoin into the world of DeFi and staking without compromising its core principles. Strategic Advantage: Unlocking the True Potential of Bitcoin in DeFi. Lombard’s value proposition is significant for one core reason: it taps into Bitcoin’s immense market, valued at over $1.5 trillion, which remains largely underutilized in DeFi due to its architectural limitations. While Ethereum's staking market has matured and captured significant traction, Bitcoin’s potential remains mostly unrealized. By enabling liquid staking and composable DeFi use cases for BTC through LBTC, Lombard is unlocking a far larger, previously inaccessible capital base. Moreover, LBTC is natively compatible with multiple ecosystems, including Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, and Sui, making it a highly flexible asset for use across various DeFi environments. Summary: Lido optimizes staking utility for a PoS-native chain (Ethereum). Lombard pioneers liquid staking for a PoW asset (Bitcoin), leveraging Babylon to safely bring BTC into PoS ecosystems. Lombard’s opportunity space, Bitcoin’s dormant DeFi capital, is significantly larger than Ethereum’s existing staking market. Kaspa ( KAS ) - Explainer What is Kaspa ( KAS )? Kaspa ( KAS ) is a revolutionary Layer-1 blockchain that utilizes a Proof-of-Work (PoW) consensus mechanism, but with an innovative GHOSTDAG protocol that significantly improves the efficiency and scalability of traditional blockchains like Bitcoin. Kaspa was launched in November 2021 and focuses on solving the scalability issues that limit other blockchains, while maintaining security and decentralization. It uses a blockDAG structure instead of the traditional linear blockchain, providing a faster and more scalable infrastructure. BlockchainInnovation How does Kaspa work? Kaspa uses the advanced GHOSTDAG technology and a blockDAG structure: GHOSTDAG protocol: Unlike traditional blockchains, which "reject" parallel blocks (orphan blocks), the GHOSTDAG protocol allows these blocks to coexist and arranges them in consensus. This increases efficiency and makes the network faster and more scalable. BlockDAG structure: Instead of a linear chain of blocks, Kaspa forms a network of blocks connected in a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). This allows multiple blocks to be processed simultaneously, increasing throughput. CryptoEcosystem The role of KAS The KAS token plays an essential role in the Kaspa ecosystem: Transaction fees: Users pay KAS for executing transactions within the network. Miners' rewards: Miners receive KAS as a reward for validating blocks and maintaining the security of the network. Network fuel: KAS serves as the fuel for the network and supports the operation of the decentralized system. Tokenomics Key features: Open-source and decentralized: Kaspa is fully open-source, meaning anyone can contribute to the development and improvement of the network. Scalability: The network is designed to scale quickly and efficiently, with plans to increase the block frequency in the future from 1 to 10 to 100 blocks per second. No premine: There was no premine or pre-reserved tokens for the team or investors, which contributes to the fair launch of the project. BlockchainProgress History and development: Foundation: Kaspa was launched in November 2021 by Yonatan Sompolinsky, a pioneer in blockchain research at Harvard, and his team. The project has a strong technical foundation with the development of the GHOSTDAG protocol. Technological innovations: Kaspa continues to develop with ongoing improvements, such as the Crescendo Hardfork, which increases the block frequency to 10 blocks per second. CryptoHistory Tokenomics Total supply: The maximum supply of KAS is 28.7 billion tokens. Circulating supply: As of April 2025, the circulating supply of KAS is approximately 25.9 to 26 billion. Emission schedule: Kaspa has a unique monetary policy that halves the reward for miners each year, but with a monthly decreasing factor that geometrically reduces the reward speed. MarketAnalysis Benefits of Kaspa: High scalability: Kaspa has the ability to process 1 block per second, with plans for even higher frequencies in the future. Secure and decentralized: The network maintains the security and decentralization of Bitcoin, but with significantly higher performance. Innovative technology: The GHOSTDAG protocol and the blockDAG structure provide an entirely new approach to blockchain technology. DeFiApplications Drawbacks and challenges: Adoption: Kaspa has not yet reached the same level of adoption as major blockchains like Ethereum or Solana, which could hinder how quickly the network grows. Competition: Kaspa competes with other Layer-1 blockchains that have already attracted more developers and users. Market volatility: The price of KAS is volatile and can fluctuate depending on broader market conditions and the adoption of the network. CryptoChallenges Applications and adoption: Kaspa is being increasingly adopted by miners and is supported by an active community. The network has potential for growth in DeFi applications and can develop into a major player in the blockchain space. Use in DeFi: Kaspa has the potential to support DeFi applications with its high processing capacity and efficient blockchain technology. Mining: Kaspa’s mining algorithm, kHeavyHash, is more energy-efficient than Bitcoin’s SHA-256, making it more environmentally friendly and accessible for miners. DeFiAdoption Price and market performance: The price of KAS is volatile, as with most altcoins. The price reached an all-time high of $0.2079 in February 2024 but has since fluctuated due to market corrections and speculations. On April 1, 2025, the price of KAS is estimated to be between $0.06 and $0.07, depending on market conditions. MarketVolatility Future outlook: The future of Kaspa depends on several factors: Technological upgrades: The Crescendo Hardfork and future scaling improvements will be crucial for further adoption of Kaspa. Adoption: Wider acceptance by users and platforms could significantly affect the price of KAS. Market trends: As with other altcoins, bull markets could push the price of KAS up, while bear markets could bring the price down. DeFiFuture Conclusion: Kaspa ( KAS ) is a promising project that combines the speed of a blockDAG with the security of Proof-of-Work. It provides a scalable, decentralized solution for the blockchain space, with an active community and technological innovations that have the potential to disrupt the blockchain market. Although there are challenges, such as adoption and competition, Kaspa remains a project to watch, especially considering its unique technology and growth potential. Is there a THREAT: AI Rewriting Itself to Crack Codes QuantumComputing Crypto CryptoAI QuantumResistance When people talk about AI cracking encryption, they often imagine a powerful AI that: 1. Analyzes encryption algorithms, 2. Redesigns its attack methods iteratively, and 3. Leverages quantum or brute-force techniques to guess private keys or signatures faster than traditional methods. AI isn't “magic,” but it accelerates attack strategies by: Testing vulnerabilities in classical cryptography (like ECDSA used in Bitcoin), Applying machine learning to find patterns in poorly implemented systems, Simulating or optimizing quantum algorithms like Shor’s or Grover’s. HOW XMSS & SPHINCS+ DEFEND AGAINST THAT Both XMSS and SPHINCS+ are hash-based signature schemes that rely on secure hash functions, like SHA-2 or SHA-3 — not number theory (like RSA or ECC) which quantum computers (and optimized AI attacks) can more easily break. 1. No Algebraic Structure to Exploit AI and quantum attacks work best when there's a math structure to exploit (like in ECC or RSA). Hash-based cryptography is structureless — it’s just a one-way avalanche of bits. So: AI can't reverse a secure hash function like SHA-256 or SHAKE-256 unless it breaks fundamental assumptions of entropy and bit collision, which is still computationally infeasible. Even quantum Grover’s algorithm only gets a square root speed-up, which means doubling the hash output length defeats it. 2. One-Time and Stateless Security (XMSS, SPHINCS+) XMSS (eXtended Merkle Signature Scheme) is stateful, meaning it keeps track of every key/signature used — each is unique and never reused. SPHINCS+ is stateless, meaning it can randomly generate keys on the fly but is slower. However, it can’t be broken by AI reverse-engineering without brute-forcing the entire tree structure. This eliminates attack surfaces: AI can't just guess the next valid signature or try a replay attack. Even if AI self-evolves, it can’t “learn” from one signature to forge another, due to their one-time or non-repeating nature. 3. Defending Against Forgery — Even by AI The attack surface for AI isn't the math — it's: Code implementation errors (bugs, leaks), Weak randomness, Poor key management. XMSS/SPHINCS+ are designed for provable security, with minimal assumptions. Even a self-rewriting AI can’t bypass: Proper key hygiene (non-reuse), Strong entropy, Cryptographic hash functions (assuming SHA-3 remains quantum-resistant with longer output sizes). If you're thinking of quantum-safe blockchain, wallet security, or long-term encrypted communication, XMSS and SPHINCS+ are your best line of defense against AI-augmented attackers, whether classical or quantum-enhanced.

GM CT, say it back It's Tacos Tuesday yet there's a confusion that won't let the Taco settle in the stomach. Ever been in a space or in a TG chat and someone says, > “That’s not a coin, it’s a token.” You smile. But deep down you’re thinking... “Wait o, aren’t they the same thing??” You’re not alone, this confusion is more common than you think. Keep reading, so next time someone says it, you won’t just smile. You’ll actually get it: ---------- Coins = Blockchain’s Native Currency A coin is a digital currency that runs on its own blockchain. If it powers the network it lives on, it's a coin. Examples: BTC (Bitcoin) → Bitcoin blockchain ETH (Ethereum) → Ethereum blockchain SOL (Solana) → Solana blockchain BNB (BNB Chain) → BNB Smart Chain Use Case: Paying gas fees Staking Sending money Network security Think of coins as the “engine oil” of a blockchain without it, nothing moves. ------------------- Tokens = Projects Built on Top of a Blockchain A token lives on an existing blockchain, it borrows the roads built by someone else. Examples: USDT → token built on Ethereum, Tron, Solana, etc. APE (ApeCoin) → built on Ethereum UNI (Uniswap) → built on Ethereum RAY (Raydium) → built on Solana Use Case: Utility (used in a specific app/project) Governance (voting power in DAOs) Store of value Rewards Tokens are like shops renting space inside a mall. The mall = the blockchain. ------------ So… ETH vs USDT vs APE? ETH = Coin → It powers Ethereum, pays gas fees USDT = Token → Stablecoin built on many chains, used for trading APE = Token → Governance + utility token in the Bored Ape ecosystem --------------- Why This Difference Matters: 1. Gas Fees: You can’t pay Ethereum gas with USDT or APE. You need ETH. Same for Solana: you need SOL to pay fees, not Raydium or USDC. 2. Security & Stability: Coins like ETH or BTC are often more secure, stable, and widely accepted. Tokens depend on the strength of the project that created them. 3. Use Case Confusion: Knowing whether something is a coin or token helps you avoid mistakes like: Trying to transfer a token without gas Holding low-utility tokens expecting coin-level growth Misunderstanding how DeFi, NFTs, and DAOs work --------------- In summary: All coins are crypto. All tokens are crypto. But not all crypto is a coin. Some power blockchains while some just exist on those blockchains. The more you understand this, the smoother your Web3 journey becomes. If you’ve ever mixed them up before now you know and if you're still learning? You're doing just fine. Have a good Taco Tuesday

Bitcoin Ideology v Austrian Economics Ideology is prescriptive and top-down. “You should (or shouldn’t) do this because it’s good (or bad) for society.” It invokes an abstract collective good and imposes moral or ethical imperatives onto individual action. It’s about what ought to be. Austrian economics is descriptive and bottom-up. “Humans act to remove felt uneasiness according to their subjective preferences.” It does not prescribe outcomes; it observes that individuals act based on what they perceive will improve their condition - not whether or not those actions are “good for society” in some ideological sense. So what follows? 1. “Fiat is bad for society” is an ideological claim. It may be true from some ethical or systemic lens, but it’s not an Austrian argument. It attempts to override individual valuation with collective judgment. 2. “People use fiat because it has subjective utility” is Austrian. Whether it’s to pay taxes, access goods, hedge volatility, or simply due to habit, their actions demonstrate their preferences. Austrianism accepts this without moralizing. 3. Therefore, a true Austrian wouldn’t say, “People should stop using fiat.” They would say: “People will stop using fiat when it no longer serves their subjective ends better than the alternatives.” Conclusion: If you’re making normative claims about fiat (or Bitcoin) being “good” or “bad” for society, you’ve stepped out of Austrian analysis and into ideological advocacy. That doesn’t make it invalid - but it’s crucial to be honest about which hat you’re wearing: economist or ideologue. Both roles have their place. Just don’t confuse the two.

British crypto investor James Howells became globally known for one of the most expensive mistakes in history—accidentally throwing away a hard drive containing passkeys to 8,000 Bitcoins, now worth nearly $8 billion. Back in 2013, Howells owned the digital assets when Bitcoin traded around $950. During a home cleanup, the hard drive was tossed in the trash and sent to a city-owned landfill in Newport, Wales. After realizing what happened, Howells tried everything to recover it. He tracked the hard drive’s likely location in the landfill and petitioned for permission to dig it up. The city refused. He took the matter to court, but the UK High Court threw out his case. By then, Bitcoin's value had skyrocketed, making the loss even more painful. His story became a cautionary tale about how fragile access to crypto wealth can be. Now, a Los Angeles-based studio, LEBUL, has secured the rights to tell Howells’ story. The planned project includes a docuseries, podcast, and short film titled “The Buried Bitcoin.” Howells says the film will detail his real-life treasure hunt, including a CGI breakdown of his high-tech plan to search the landfill. Despite the setbacks and plans to close the landfill, Howells insists he’s not giving up. He's even expressed interest in buying the site.

Q: What is the essence of JoyPlay? A: First, JoyPlay is a GameFi platform focused on the BTC ecosystem. Second, JoyPlay is not just a simple blockchain game—it is a blockchain-based platform that integrates gaming, finance, and social interaction. Lastly, JoyPlay adheres to the core spirit of decentralization and is driven by a long-term vision of ecological development. Q: What is JoyPlay’s platform economic structure like? A: As we all know, the fusion of blockchain gaming and finance—starting from projects like Axie and up to StepN—once became a major vertical in the blockchain space. With strong trading features, DeFi found powerful leverage on the soil of GameFi. However, with the proliferation of such games, the economic models of DeFi-enhanced games became increasingly aggressive and eventually revealed a fatal flaw: they often entered a “death spiral.” So, JoyPlay takes a different path. One of the most important features of JoyPlay’s token economy is that there is no ICO or IDO. Tokens are only generated through playing games and staking NFTs. Other than a limited amount of NFTs available for purchase in the early stage, nearly all NFTs must be bought with tokens. NFTs also have a decay period, and will be burned after the staking period ends. This creates a healthy dual-cycle economic structure. An innovative aspect of JoyPlay’s system is that every time a player plays a game, energy is consumed. And this energy is obtained by staking NFTs. Q: How are JoyPlay’s social features presented? A: This is another innovative aspect of JoyPlay. As we mentioned before, JoyPlay is not a standalone game—it is a game ecosystem platform, meaning it includes substantial ecological content. We already covered the role of energy in gameplay and how it's obtained by staking NFTs. For users who hold OG cards and have staked NFTs, sharing game content on their personal Twitter accounts will be analyzed by AI, which will evaluate the content quality and engagement. Based on this, users will receive points rewards and energy bonuses for participating in social sharing and content creation. Weekly, users who rank in the Top 100 in points, as well as those who make special contributions in the social module, will receive NFT fragment airdrops. These fragments can be assembled into complete NFTs, which can then be staked. Additionally, in blockchain, DeFi and social elements are inherently intertwined. New users who come from shared social links will be grouped under the inviter’s network, enabling the inviter to earn passive income from NFT staking rewards generated by their network. Q: You mentioned OG cards earlier. What role do OG cards play on the platform? A: OG cards are a badge for early-stage ecosystem builders. A: OG cards are only issued to early community contributors and builders. There will only ever be 10,000 OG cards, and no more will be minted regardless of how JoyPlay develops in the future. Q: How many games will JoyPlay have in the future, and what types will they be? A: Within 5 to 6 months, the platform will launch around 5 games, aiming to complete Phase 1 of content balancing. After that, based on community feedback and OG cardholder governance voting, the platform will expand to meet market demands. Of the initial 5 games, one is competitive, and the other four are either PVP or PVE oriented. Q: Why did you choose to build JoyPlay on the BTC ecosystem? A: Decentralization has always been the essence and core of blockchain. It's undeniable that ecosystems like BSC, TRON, the rising TON, and the ever-popular SOL offer better development environments for blockchain games. However, the BTC ecosystem remains the most original and inherently decentralized chain. With an increasing number of builders working on both the protocol and transaction layers of BTC, we are proud to be the first GameFi ecosystem platform under the BTC and BRC2.0 protocol layer. Our ambition is to become the most successful GameFi content platform in the future of the Bitcoin ecosystem.

I remember being in a world where ATMs weren’t even common. To get money, you had to stand in line at the bank, sometimes for hours. Then came ATMs. Suddenly, withdrawing cash was easier, but spending still meant carrying physical money. Later, transfers became the norm. You could pay for things with your phone. No need for cash but you still needed a bank. Now, I live in a world where crypto is slowly becoming currency. It's still growing, still limited in daily use but the vision is clear: Money is changing. Forever. In some countries, crypto is now a real currency just like dollars, euros, or naira. You can actually use it to buy things, pay for services, or send money to someone in another country in seconds. Here are 6 cryptocurrencies that are now used as currency in some countries or platforms. Bitcoin (BTC) This is the original crypto, the one that started it all. People call it “digital gold” because it holds value like gold but you can send it anywhere instantly. In some places, you can pay for groceries or coffee with it. Seriously. Nobody owns it (it’s run by the people, for the people). Created by the legendary (and anonymous) Satoshi Nakamoto. Ethereum (ETH) If Bitcoin is digital gold, Ethereum is the internet of money. It’s what apps, games, and NFTs run on. You can use it to pay, invest, or interact with smart contracts like mini-programs that do things automatically. Created by Vitalik Buterin and team around 2015. Tether (USDT) This one’s super useful. It’s always equal to $1, so there are no price swings like Bitcoin. You can send and receive money quickly, especially in countries where the local currency keeps dropping. It’s run by a company, so it’s not as “people-powered,” but it works. Created by A company called Tether Limited. BNB (Binance Coin) BNB was created by Binance, one of the biggest crypto platforms. You can use it to get discounts, pay for services, or even shop with certain crypto cards. It’s more like a VIP pass to the Binance world. Solana (SOL) Solana is super fast and cheap to use. It’s big in NFTs and online games, where you can earn and spend real money. If you’re into tech or digital art, solana worth knowing. Created by Solana Labs (led by Anatoly Yakovenko) USD Coin (USDC) This is another stable coin always worth $1, but more regulated and transparent than Tether. Great for businesses, online payments, and saving without worrying about the price going up and down. Created by The U.S. fintech company Circle, with help from Coinbase.

𝐔𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐋𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠: 𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐁𝐢𝐭𝐜𝐨𝐢𝐧 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐬 𝐅𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐂𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐩 The Lightning Network (LN) isn’t just a speed boost for Bitcoin,it’s a full-on transformation of how BTC payments happen. But beneath the surface of instant sats and low fees lies one of the most complex processes in the ecosystem: routing. Let’s break it down mah people. ———————————————— 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠? When you send Bitcoin via the Lightning Network, you're not sending it directly on the Bitcoin blockchain. Instead, you're using payment channels,like tunnels between users that let funds travel instantly and off-chain. But not everyone is directly connected. So, to pay someone you don’t have a channel with, your payment needs to route through other people’s open channels. Think of it like this: → You’re in Lagos and want to send a package to someone in Abuja. → You don’t have a direct bus. → So you route it through Ibadan → Ilorin → Minna → Abuja. That’s what Lightning routing does,finding a path from sender to receiver using channels with enough liquidity and trust. ———————————————— 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐋𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 Liquidity Matters: If a middle channel doesn’t have enough satoshis on the right side, your payment fails. Fees Vary: Each node charges a routing fee. The longer the route, the more you might pay. Privacy vs Pathfinding: Unlike traditional payment systems, Lightning wants privacy. So routing doesn’t always reveal the entire network topology, which can make it harder to find the best route. Dynamic Conditions: Network conditions change fast. A route that worked a second ago might fail now. ———————————————— 𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐃𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐤 𝐢𝐧 𝐏𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐞? → Your wallet checks the network for possible paths. → It calculates the best route,balancing fees, speed, and liquidity. → It uses HTLCs (Hashed Timelock Contracts) to lock the payment conditionally at each hop. → Once the receiver claims the payment, all intermediate nodes are paid instantly. → If it fails at any point, the funds return to you. ———————————————— 𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐍𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐬 𝐄𝐚𝐫𝐧 𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 Routing isn’t charity,nodes make money by forwarding payments. → Each node can set a base fee (fixed per payment) and a fee rate (percentage of the amount routed). → By maintaining good liquidity and uptime, nodes become more attractive for routing. → Power users and node operators can actually earn a decent yield by optimizing channel balancing. ———————————————— 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐃𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐑𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐌𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐁𝐢𝐭𝐜𝐨𝐢𝐧’𝐬 𝐅𝐮𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞? Without efficient routing, the Lightning Network can’t scale. Imagine millions of micro-payments,from streaming sats to in-game rewards,happening per second. That only works if routing is: Fast Reliable Cheap Routing is the plumbing of Lightning, and the smoother it gets, the more BTC can become truly programmable money. ———————————————— 𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐓𝐚𝐤𝐞 In Nigeria and across Africa, where traditional banking can be slow, expensive, or unavailable, routing on the Lightning Network opens new possibilities. It allows anyone with a smartphone and a Lightning wallet to send and receive BTC like text messages.

Day 3/5 ~ Unpacking Confirmations ~ How chains model finality, and why your app needs to think probabilistically ~ yesterday, we explored how “confirmation” depends on the chain. Today, let’s unpack how those chains actually model finality, and why your app needs to move beyond a binary view of “confirmed vs not" Most chains don’t offer a single clean answer. Instead, you’re working with a spectrum: 1. deterministic finality: chains using BFT-style consensus (e.g. cosms, some alt-DAs), L1 settlement (e.g. ethereu after finality) and most PoS offer hard guarantees - once finalized, a transaction can’t be reverted. 2. probabilistic finality: pow chains (like bitcoin) and ethereum "pre-finality" offer statistical guarantees. A tx buried 12 blocks deep is unlikely to be reorged - but not impossible. the deeper, the safer. 3. soft signals: sequencer confirmations, mempool inclusion, builder relays - they’re fast, but carry risk. these signals are useful, but must be treated carefully. apps often treat these sources equally: → “wait X blocks” → “trust the sequencer” → “check for inclusion” But that abstraction breaks as soon as you go interop. A cross-chain app might span: ~ A fast-finality BFT chain ~ An optimistic rollup with 7-day fraud windows ~ An L1 with probabilistic finality ~ A chain with sequencer-only guarantees your app logic can’t hardcode a one-size-fits-all rule. you need to ask: “How likely is this tx to revert? And who enforces that?” ==> finality isn’t binary and the tradeoff between speed and security isn’t linear. (multisigs, for example, don’t gain speed or trust.) → what you need is programmable, chain-aware confidence == a way to express what “confirmed” means in each context

Union Consensus is now portable. Before Union, consensus was siloed. Ethereum knew its own state, but not Cosmos’s. Guide to STRF, STRK, and STRD Strategy has issued 3 perpetual preferred stock offerings, all of which differ in their dividend rates, convertibility, seniority, and risk profiles, designed to appeal to different types of investors. Dividend Rates and Structure: STRF: Offers a 10% fixed annual dividend based on a $100 liquidation preference, paid quarterly starting June 30, 2025. If dividends are missed, the rate compounds at an additional 1% per year, up to a maximum of 18%, incentivizing timely payments. The dividends are cumulative, meaning unpaid dividends accrue and must be paid before common stock dividends. STRK: Provides an 8% fixed annual dividend based on a $100 liquidation preference, also paid quarterly. Like STRF, dividends are cumulative, increasing if unpaid. However, the effective yield may decrease as the stock price rises due to its conversion feature. STRD: Pays a higher yield (approximately 11.7% at a price of $85), but its dividends are non-cumulative, meaning missed payments do not accrue, making it riskier. The exact dividend rate is not specified in the provided data, but it’s noted as higher than STRF and STRK. Convertibility: STRF: No conversion option. It functions as a fixed-income security, prioritizing stable income and capital stability, appealing to investors seeking predictable returns without equity upside. STRK: Includes a conversion feature, allowing holders to convert each share into 0.1 shares of Strategy’s common stock (MSTR) if MSTR reaches $1,000 per share. This offers potential capital appreciation, making it a hybrid between a bond-like security and equity. It’s more correlated to MSTR’s performance, especially as MSTR nears $1,000. STRD: No conversion option, similar to STRF. It’s designed as a high-yield security, akin to a junk bond, focusing on income over equity upside. Seniority in Capital Structure: All three are perpetual preferred stocks, sitting between debt and common equity in Strategy’s capital structure, meaning they have priority over common shares (MSTR) in liquidation but are subordinate to senior debt. STRK: Appears to rank senior to STRF and STRD in liquidation priority. STRF: Ranks in the middle of the preferred stock hierarchy. STRD: The most junior of the three, carrying higher risk in a liquidation scenario. Risk and Investor Appeal: STRF: Considered investment-grade due to its cumulative dividends and lack of conversion, offering lower volatility and more predictable returns. It’s ideal for income-focused investors who prioritize stability. STRK: Balances yield and growth potential due to its conversion feature, appealing to investors seeking both income and exposure to MSTR’s upside, particularly if Bitcoin performs well. It’s riskier than STRF but less risky than STRD. STRD: Labeled as junk-grade due to non-cumulative dividends and junior status, offering higher yield but greater risk. It’s suited for risk-tolerant investors seeking high income, with less protection if Strategy faces financial distress. Offering Size and Market Performance: STRF: Raised approximately $711.2 million by selling 8.5 million shares at $85 each, exceeding its initial $500 million target. It’s designed to fund Bitcoin acquisitions and general corporate purposes. STRK: Initially raised $563.4 million, with an upsized offering from $250 million to $584 million, though it launched at a discounted $80 per share (20% below $100 par value). Since February 1, 2025, STRK has gained +6%, outperforming MSTR (-16.44%) and Bitcoin (-19%). STRD: Had the largest offering, upsized from 2.5 million to 11.76 million shares, raising $999.9 million. At the 2025 Bitcoin Economy Conference in Las Vegas, hosted by HouseofZK, Robin Linus unveiled something that could redefine Bitcoin scalability called BitVM3. Building on the earlier versions of BitVM, this new iteration takes a giant leap forward introducing garbled circuits to optimize fraud proofs. Shortly after his presentation, Robin published the first BitVM3 paper, laying the foundation for what’s now becoming a breakthrough powered by goatnetwork. Originally, when Robin introduced BitVM2, it was seen as a revolutionary concept but not immediately practical. Its script sizes reached around 1GB, making it difficult to post fraud proofs without relying on non-standard transactions (NSTs), which Bitcoin doesn’t support by default. Here is a breakdown of the secure and efficient flow of bringing BTC onto BOB using wrapped assets and intent-based execution 1) Liquidity commitment by LPs :- Liquidity Providers (LPs) lock wrapped Bitcoin (WBTC or tBTC) into BOB’s escrow smart contracts. This liquidity becomes available for Bitcoin users wanting to access DeFi on BOB. 2) User signals intent :- A user requests to reserve liquidity by sending a signal to the off-chain relayer, specifying how they want to use their BTC (e.g. minting LSTs, staking, or swapping). 3) BTC transaction with embedded order :- The user sends native BTC to the LP’s Bitcoin address. Inside the transaction’s OP_RETURN, a hash of the user's order is embedded, including Their EVM wallet address on BOB Their intent (e.g. strategy like minting LST or LRT) This makes the users intent on-chain verifiable no oracle required. 4) Trustless verification via Merkle proofs :- The relayer submits a Merkle proof of the BTC transaction to BOB on-chain Bitcoin light client. This trustlessly confirms the transaction on Bitcoin and authorizes the relayer to access the matching wrapped BTC on BOB. 5) Intent fulfillment on BOB :- The gateway now executes the user’s request Sends wrapped BTC to the user’s EVM address Mints LST/LRT tokens if requested All actions are driven by the user’s original Bitcoin transaction aligning execution with their intent. No Bridges. No Oracles. Just Pure Cryptographic Verification.
